es: Escribir un relato propio con escena mostrada, ritmo controlado, giro, desenlace y un toque de humor o ironía.

teaching.en: A good story opens with a scene, not a summary: rain tapped the window while Tom counted his keys.
teaching.es: Un buen relato abre con una escena, no con un resumen: la lluvia golpeaba la ventana mientras Tom contaba sus llaves.
teaching.explanationEs: Mostrar la escena con detalles concretos engancha más que contar «Tom estaba nervioso».
segments: A good story opens with a scene, not a summary:
rain tapped the window while Tom counted his keys.
teaching.audioText: A good story opens with a scene, not a summary: rain tapped the window while Tom counted his keys.

teaching.en: Short fragments quicken the pace: Down the hill ran the dog. Silence.
teaching.es: Los fragmentos cortos aceleran el ritmo: Colina abajo corrió el perro. Silencio.
teaching.explanationEs: La anteposición (Down the hill ran…) y las frases sin verbo controlan la velocidad del relato.
segments: Short fragments quicken the pace: Down
the hill ran the dog. Silence.
teaching.audioText: Short fragments quicken the pace: Down the hill ran the dog. Silence.

teaching.en: The twist arrives late: the letter she feared all week is an invitation.
teaching.es: El giro llega tarde: la carta que temió toda la semana es una invitación.
teaching.explanationEs: El giro cambia lo que el lector creía; conviene preparar la sospecha antes con detalles.
segments: The twist arrives late: the letter she
feared all week is an invitation.
teaching.audioText: The twist arrives late: the letter she feared all week is an invitation.

teaching.en: Details reveal feelings: his hands shook as he folded the map.
teaching.es: Los detalles revelan los sentimientos: le temblaban las manos mientras doblaba el mapa.
teaching.explanationEs: Mostrar la emoción con una acción (shook) evita nombrarla; era lo visto en «Show, don't tell».
segments: Details reveal feelings: his hands shook
teaching.audioText: Details reveal feelings: his hands shook as he folded the map.

teaching.en: A satisfying ending answers the question the story raised at the start.
teaching.es: Un desenlace satisfactorio responde a la pregunta que planteó el principio del relato.
teaching.explanationEs: El final cierra el círculo: lo que se preguntaba al empezar recibe respuesta.
segments: A satisfying ending answers the question
the story raised at the start.
teaching.audioText: A satisfying ending answers the question the story raised at the start.

teaching.en: A touch of irony helps: the taxi, of course, arrived after the wedding.
teaching.es: Un toque de ironía ayuda: el taxi, por supuesto, llegó después de la boda.
teaching.explanationEs: Of course dicho de algo que ocurre al revés de lo esperado es ironía amable; sin burla.
segments: A touch of irony helps: the taxi,
of course, arrived after the wedding.
teaching.audioText: A touch of irony helps: the taxi, of course, arrived after the wedding.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase muestra el nerviosismo sin nombrarlo?

choices.text: Her hands shook as she folded the map.
She felt nervous about the map.

feedback.es: Una acción concreta (las manos que tiemblan) deja ver el nervio; las otras frases solo lo etiquetan.

hint.es: Busca el detalle físico, no la etiqueta de la emoción.

prompt.es: Ordena con anteposición: «En la habitación entró un desconocido.»

answer.text: Into the room walked a stranger

feedback.es: Con anteposición, el lugar va primero y el sujeto sigue al verbo: Into the room walked a stranger.

hint.es: Empieza por el lugar; el sujeto va detrás del verbo.

prompt.es: Completa: «Al abrir la carta, entendió que había perdido el concurso.»

feedback.es: Perder el concurso ocurrió antes de abrir la carta: se marca con had + participio.

hint.es: Lo ocurrido antes del momento de abrir la carta necesita un auxiliar.

origin.text: When she opened the letter, she understood that she ___ lost the contest.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es el giro de este relato breve?

choices.text: Mia refuses to read the letter.
The feared letter is really good news.

feedback.es: El giro cambia lo que el lector esperaba: la carta temida resulta ser una invitación.

origin.text: All week Mia feared the letter from the council. On Friday it arrived: an invitation to her own surprise party.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo trata el narrador la excusa del fontanero.

choices.text: The narrator is ironic about the excuse.
The narrator praises the plumber sincerely.
The narrator describes a flood without humour.

feedback.es: «Of course it was not» dice lo contrario de lo que piensa el narrador: es ironía.

origin.audio: The plumber promised to arrive at nine. He arrived at noon, just after the flood, and kindly explained that the delay was not his fault. Of course it was not.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del relato con su función.

pairs: Down the hill ran the dog.
She smiled, at last, and stayed.
The bus, of course, was late.

feedback.es: Cada frase cumple una función distinta en la estructura del relato: mostrar, acelerar, sorprender, cerrar y sonreír.

pairs: Down the hill ran the dog.
She smiled, at last, and stayed.
The bus, of course, was late.

prompt.es: Completa: «Tom, por supuesto, volvió a olvidar las llaves.»

feedback.es: Of course, dicho del fallo habitual de alguien, introduce una ironía amable.

origin.text: Tom, of ___, forgot his keys again.

prompt.es: ¿Qué versión usa fragmentos para acelerar el ritmo?

choices.text: The door was opened and footsteps were heard and then nothing was there.
The door opened. Footsteps. Then nothing.
The door opened, and then there were footsteps, and finally there was nothing.

feedback.es: Las frases cortas y sin verbo (Footsteps. Then nothing.) aceleran el ritmo; las otras lo alargan con y.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cuál es el giro del relato.

choices.text: The neighbour asks her for money.
The neighbour returns her lost wallet.

feedback.es: Sara creía que el vecino era un problema, pero venía a devolverle su cartera: ese cambio es el giro.

origin.audio: For a week Sara hid from the neighbour who kept knocking on her door. On Friday she finally opened it, and he handed her a lost wallet with her whole week's pay inside.

prompt.es: Escribe tu relato: escena, ritmo, giro, desenlace e ironía (unas 150 palabras).

answer.text: Rain tapped the window of the bus. Leo checked his watch for the fifth time, tapping his foot on the wet floor. On his knees lay the folder with his drawings, and his hands would not stay still. The driver hummed a cheerful song, which made everything worse. Off the bus he jumped, and up the stairs he ran. Silence in the corridor. A closed door. He had missed the interview by ten minutes, and he had practised his speech for a week. Then a woman appeared at the end of the hall, holding a cup of tea. "Are you Leo?" she asked. "We had to postpone everything. The director, of course, is stuck in traffic." Leo laughed so loudly that the secretary looked up. She offered him a cup of tea, and he drank it slowly. In the end, he got the job. The director arrived an hour later, blaming the bus.
accepted: Rain tapped the window of the bus. Leo checked his watch for the fifth time, tapping his foot on the wet floor. On his knees lay the folder with his drawings, and his hands would not stay still. The driver hummed a cheerful song, which made everything worse. Off the bus he jumped, and up the stairs he ran. Silence in the corridor. A closed door. He had missed the interview by ten minutes, and he had practised his speech for a week. Then a woman appeared at the end of the hall, holding a cup of tea. "Are you Leo?" she asked. "We had to postpone everything. The director, of course, is stuck in traffic." Leo laughed so loudly that the secretary looked up. She offered him a cup of tea, and he drank it slowly. In the end, he got the job. The director arrived an hour later, blaming the bus.

Every Sunday my grandfather used to fish at the lake, and every Sunday he came home with an empty bucket and a happy face. My mother would laugh and say that fishing was only an excuse to sit in silence. One morning I followed him. Into the water went his line, and out of the silence came nothing. Hours passed, and the lake stayed as silent as a painting. Then a tiny silver fish jumped into the bucket by itself. My grandfather stared at it. "Unbelievable," he whispered. His hands shook a little as he held the bucket. I had never seen him so excited, or so suspicious. "Of course," he said at last, "the day I bring a friend, the fish behave." In the end, he let the fish go and told everybody it was the best catch of his life. Since then, he has never fished alone.

feedback.es: Un relato completo muestra la escena, controla el ritmo, prepara un giro, cierra con un desenlace y suma una ironía amable.

origin.text: Cuenta una historia corta con: una escena mostrada con detalles, una anteposición o fragmentos, un giro, un desenlace y un toque de humor o ironía.

prompt.es: Convierte «Tom was nervous.» en una frase que muestre el nerviosismo.

answer.text: Tom's hands shook as he opened the door.
accepted: Tom's hands shook as he opened the door.
Tom's hands were shaking as he opened the door.
Tom kept tapping his foot on the floor.
Tom bit his lip and checked his watch again.

feedback.es: Mostrar es sustituir la etiqueta (nervous) por un gesto observable, como tapping o shook.

prompt.es: Ordena el cierre: «Al final, nadie dijo una palabra.»

answer.text: In the end, nobody said a word

feedback.es: In the end abre el desenlace y el verbo va en pasado simple, como el resto de la acción.

choices.text: The bus, of course, left just as I reached the stop.
The bus left as I reached the stop.

feedback.es: Of course marca la ironía: el narrador dice que era previsible lo que en realidad le fastidia.
